annotation.title_clean: Ghana (Insights on Public Policies to Ensure AI's Beneficial Use as a Professional Tool)
annotation.title_en: Ghana (Insights on Public Policies to Ensure AI's Beneficial Use as a Professional Tool)
annotation.venue: IBA Alternative and New Law Business Structures Committee
named_instruments_referenced: Legal Profession (Professional Conduct and Etiquette) Rules 2020
annotation.summary_en: Ghana country chapter in an IBA questionnaire-style report on AI in legal services. It finds no statutory AI definition, regulatory framework or AI legal tools in use. It reviews data protection, copyright and privacy case law as applicable, and notes calls for an ethical and regulatory AI framework.
key_provisions_or_claims: Ghana has no statutory definition of AI and no AI-specific regulatory framework.
Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843) requires consent and lawful processing of personal data used in AI.
Constitutional privacy right and the Cubagee Supreme Court case reinforce consent for data use.
Legal profession rules contain no AI provisions but confidentiality duties apply.
Government and stakeholders acknowledge need for ethical and regulatory AI framework.
